motion.name: landing-depth
motion.purpose: Independent hero scene and parallax progress over native scroll at every viewport size. The hero uses a 180svh section with a sticky 100svh stage. Pause and reduced motion restore static flow. Scroll transforms are separate from the hero identity renderer and its transition-only RAF; Work uses its own 0.45s progress controller.

motion.name: scene-wordmark-pulse
motion.purpose: Owner-approved orange 3D sign: emissive intensity 1.2 + 0.6 * pulse; warm point-light intensity 200 + 90 * pulse. This scene effect does not apply to flat UI controls.

motion.name: relationship-wall
motion.value: Three linear CSS transform loops: right 130s / left 140s / right 125s; delays: -28s / -16s / -24s; identical duplicated runs translate between -50% and 0; edge fades: 12% desktop / 7% mobile; positive scroll-speed impulse: at most 2.25x, 160ms attack, 1.1s return to 1x, power2.out
motion.purpose: Compact brand wall in native vertical flow. Each row repeats its assigned marks twice per run, then duplicates the run for a seamless loop. All 40 visual copies are aria-hidden; a canonical semantic list retains ten names and accurate relationship captions. Passive native scroll uses absolute velocity to add a bounded speed impulse through short existing-GSAP tweens and Animation.updatePlaybackRate, preserving phase and the right/left/right directions. An IntersectionObserver and document-visibility listener gate CSS play state, pausing offscreen or hidden. Offscreen, hidden and cleanup states cancel rate tweens and reset the rate to 1x. No brand ScrollTrigger, custom animation-frame loop, sticky stage, perspective, skew or scroll-driven position. Pause/reduced motion/no JavaScript shows the complete four-/two-column grid; during motion it is visually clipped while remaining accessible. No brand progress bar; the global indicator hides while Brands is active.

motion.name: booking-open
motion.purpose: Native calendar dialog entry. Global reduced-motion rules override durations to 0.001ms and animation iteration count to one.

motion.name: hero-identity
motion.value: First start: 650ms; transition: 1120ms; alternating starts: every 5000ms of active visible time
motion.purpose: One lazy native WebGL quad with registered opaque plates, textured reveal, luminance-derived refraction/ripples, local temporal tears and chromatic split. Clean settled endpoints; timers sleep between transitions, offscreen/hidden rendering pauses and DPR caps at 1.5. Motion-off/reduced/no-JS/GPU or asset failure/context loss preserve the server astronaut poster.

motion.name: work-film-sequence
motion.value: GSAP ScrollTrigger scrub: 0.45, ease: none; stage: 280svh with sticky 100svh; opposing vertical travel: 112svh desktop / 80svh mobile; internal crop counter-travel: 16%; independent title travel: 12svh; perspective: 1500px
motion.purpose: One reversible progress value controls both film planes, crop counter-parallax, title and paused currentTime. Desktop adds opposing 8vw horizontal travel, yaw/rotation and central depth lifts up to 70px/50px; mobile retains vertical travel and rotation. Layout refresh explicitly restores progress and frames. IntersectionObserver loads sources within one viewport of the stage; no initial-hero requests or idle/offscreen/hidden seeks. One seek per video is in flight, with the latest target applied on seeked. Pause/reduced/no-JS/error states retain composed posters; no-JS and cold reduced mode request no videos. The real Maestro/GymTree proof links follow in normal flow.

narrative.northStar: A Personal Introduction Suspended in Space
narrative.overview:
The landing and playable cockpit share monumental Unbounded interface
titles, Space Grotesk text and actions, warm ivory on near-black, orange commands and thin
rectangular frames. The accepted landing supplies the visual authority for
this shared system. Dungyov informs the outlined/solid lettering; Oakley
Axiom Space informs media scale and native-scroll depth, not asset identity.

The hero alternates between matched photographic portraits of Matteo and
his astronaut alter ego through a brief, localized optical glitch. The toy
character connects these portraits to the existing Three.js model. Two
opposing film planes introduce the real app cards in Work. A natural
photographic avatar and services portrait share
one edit of the owner’s real photograph.
The landing is spacious and direct; the cockpit is playful and
instrument-dense. Flat controls, the shared avatar and equal EN/IT treatment
connect them while scrolling and gameplay retain their functional layouts.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black space, warm ivory text and orange actions.
Shared Unbounded interface titles and Space Grotesk prose and actions.
Thin rectangular frames, flat controls and restrained two-pixel corners.
Matched human/astronaut portraits, a consistent toy character and recognizable identity.
Native-scroll depth on the landing; readable telemetry in the playable CV.

rules.name: The Shared Identity Rule
rules.body:
Use the same palette, display/body roles and
flat control language across both routes; reserve signal colors for working
instruments and status.

rules.name: The Type Roles Rule
rules.body:
Use Unbounded for interface titles, Space Grotesk
for reading and actions, and JetBrains Mono for telemetry and code on
either surface. Preserve the explicitly approved Helvetiker 3D sign.

rules.name: The Flat Controls Rule
rules.body:
Use fill, hairline borders and clear state
changes for interface depth; keep physical light in the space scene.

rules.name: The Optional Motion Rule
rules.body:
Readable content and usable navigation are
the base layer; depth travel enhances them without intercepting scrolling.

dos: Do share Unbounded interface titles, Space Grotesk reading/actions and JetBrains Mono telemetry/code across landing and cockpit, preserving the approved orange Helvetiker 3D sign.
Do use thin frames, flat controls and small control corners across both routes, with outline/solid display contrast on the landing.
Do preserve keyboard focus, native anchors, readable content and reduced-motion behavior in both languages.
Do preserve the toy character across the existing cockpit model and original generated landing artwork, with recorded provenance.
Do use the matching natural avatar and services portrait derived from the owner’s photograph, alongside actual shipped product imagery.
Do retain official logo provenance, relationship captions and complete static access to the wall's ten items, distinguishing personal work from clients.
Do confine the identity glitch to its registered subject plates, keep clean settled photographs and preserve the composed astronaut fallback.
donts: Don't restore the orbit brand symbol, service-row icons or raw GLB renders as landing artwork.
Don't restore the separate Orbitron/Rajdhani interface font system or decorative chrome glow, scanlines and metal fasteners. The restored emissive 3D sign is an explicit scene exception.
Don't turn HUD signal colors into general marketing accents or monospace telemetry styles into body and action typography.
Don't make reading or contact depend on animation, JavaScript or completing the cockpit.
Don't confuse a booking-link click with a completed appointment or confirmed lead.
